text: Turn intended outcomes into checkable criteria.

Begin with what stakeholders need. Express each required result as a clear condition that can be assessed. In this guide's wording, 'must' marks an obligation; other traditions may use 'shall'. In the workshop scoring model, 'should' marks an improvement that earns optional points. A useful requirement is justified, understandable, possible to meet, verifiable, and connected to the original need.

items: State the stakeholder need. You should see: A plain outcome. If not: Ask what problem needs solving.
Write one measurable obligation. You should see: One condition per requirement. If not: Remove vague words or mixed requirements.
Choose evidence for that obligation. You should see: A possible check. If not: Rewrite a condition that cannot be checked.
Illustration: A support platform needs three distinct methods for retrieving disabled equipment. A fourth method may improve its workshop rating.

text: Each requirement connects a need to an implementation and evidence.
Check every non-negotiable condition before putting a value on desirable additions.
A mandatory condition cannot be traded away because another feature scores well.
